2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of the case are that, the opposite party as plaintiff instituted a suit in the Court of the Assistant Judge and Family Court, Kutubdia, Cox's Bazar being Family Court Suit No. 3 of 1984, claiming dower and maintenance and ultimately obtained a decree therein on contest on 28-11-94 for an amount of Taka 10000.00 as dower and Taka 11,800.00 as maintenance. Subsequently, on the prayer of the petitioner judgment-debtor, the learned Family Court by his order dated 11-11-97 allowed installments for payment of the decretal dues by the judgment debtor. Thereafter the plaintiff opposite party filed an application before the learned Family Court praying for realisation of the decretal dues at a time on the ground of hardships whereupon the learned Family Court by his order dated 5-2-98 revised his earlier order and directed the judgment debtor petitioner to pay Taka 30,000.00 at it time as dower money and to pay Taka 10000.00 per month for the balance of the decretal dues. 

 6. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has placed before us the impugned orders. It appears that the learned Family Court on due consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case rescheduled the order of installments for payment of the decretal dues in exercise of his discretionary power confirmed by section 17(5) of the Family Courts Ordinance, 1985. The learned Family Court is never bound to allow installments to the judgment debtor but still then the Court was pleased to allow installments to the judgment-debtor petitioner on consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case. Thereafter on the prayer of the decree-holder plaintiff the learned Family Court reconsidered his earlier order for payment of the decretal dues by installments and modified his earlier order on the representation of the decree-holder, it is against this re-scheduling of installments the judgment-debtor petitioner filed the present case and challenged the same as being illegal and arbitrary. 

 7. In the facts of the case, it is dearly found that the learned Family Court in exercise of his discretion allowed payment, of the decretal dues by the judgment-debtor petitioner by installments but subsequently rescheduled the mode of payment by the impugned order on the representation of the plaintiff decree-holder on the ground of hardships. It is thus dearly found that the learned Family Court passed the impugned order rescheduling the mode of payment of the decretal dues by the petitioner in exercise of his judicial discretion. In the facts and circumstances of the case we do not find any illegality or legal infirmity in the impugned order occasioning failure of justice so as to justify interference by this Court exercising revisional power under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. It is to be dearly noted in this connection that the judgment-debtor in a Family Courts case is never entitled to installments in payment of the decretal dues as a matter of right but only as a matter of grace as may be allowed by the Family Court under given circumstances. The judgment-debtor can never claim it as of right. The impugned order appears to be quite reasonable and equitable causing no prejudice to the defendant petitioner. We, therefore, find no substance in the revision.
